key_insight: Routinely collected EHR data can pre-populate VTE risk assessments with machine learning, matching clinician-recorded variables closely enough to support real-time documentation.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce clinician paperwork while preserving the clinical validity of inpatient VTE risk assessment workflows.
method: Analyzed 577,904 admissions and 726,896 VTE assessment forms across five NHS hospitals (2015–2025).
Compared form completion, timing, and concordance with structured EHR data in 87,118 assessments from 2023–2024.
Built ML models using EHR-derived versus clinician-recorded risk factors in 74,372 encounters completed within 14 hours of admission.
evidence_signal: Assessment completion was 96.7%, timely completion rose from 47.4% in 2015 to 90.5% in 2024, and EHR-derived models achieved AUROC 0.709 versus 0.704 for clinician-recorded variables.
watch_item: Some important low-prevalence risk factors were under-documented in forms, so automated pre-population still needs careful local validation and workflow integration.
paper_title: Machine Learning-Supported Efficient VTE Risk Assessment using Routinely Collected Electronic Health Record Data
